rounds.text: Shraddha Prime Projects Ltd trades at an attractive P/E multiple of 11.8x [E1], which sits well below the sector benchmark of 22.38x [E6]. The business demonstrates exceptional operational and capital efficiency, boasting a three-year median return on equity of 43% [E21] and a recent ROE of 51.2% [E13], vastly outperforming the sector benchmark of 4.26% [E9]. Growth has been explosive, highlighted by a 290% compounded sales growth rate over three years [E14] and a 376% compounded profit growth rate over the same period [E16]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow valuation estimates intrinsic value at Rs 560 per share against a market price of Rs 165 [E36], offering a substantial margin of safety of 70.5% [E37]. The market's current pricing is remarkably conservative, with a reverse DCF indicating that the share price implies a mere 1.1% earnings growth [E38]. Conceded: operating cash flow is negative at Rs -38 Cr and cash conversion sits at -0.72x for March 2026 [E28, E27].

Shraddha Prime Projects Ltd carries heavy financial risks that are masked by its headline profitability metrics. Most critically, the company reported negative operating cash flow of Rs -38 Cr and free cash flow of Rs -39 Cr in March 2026, resulting in an alarming cash conversion ratio of -0.72x against reported profit [E27, E28, E29]. This severe disconnect is compounded by a flagged negative indicating that the company might be capitalizing its interest cost [E47]. Leverage is also elevated, with debt-to-equity at 1.98x as total borrowings climbed to Rs 262 Cr in March 2026, meaning debt exceeds net worth and creates tangible balance sheet risk [E30, E32]. Furthermore, operational momentum is showing cracks: the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends are both rated as inconsistent, earnings growth has explicitly been flagged as decelerating, and the 1-year compounded share price growth sits at -11% with the stock trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E25, E26, E41, E53]. Conceded: the company displays strong historical sales and profit growth alongside high return on equity metrics, and trades at a price-to-earnings ratio well below the sector benchmark [E6, E9, E14, E16].

Conceded: operating cash flow was negative at Rs -38 Cr and free cash flow was negative at Rs -39 Cr for March 2026 [E28, E29], and it is flagged that the company might be capitalizing its interest cost [E47]. However, this short-term cash flow pressure occurs alongside an otherwise exceptionally robust financial and operating profile, including a comfortable current ratio of 2.14x ensuring solid short-term liquidity [E31]. The concern over leverage and rising borrowings up to Rs 262 Cr [E32] is heavily outweighed by stellar returns on capital and equity, featuring an ROE of 40.8% and an ROCE of 19.97% that vastly outperform sector benchmarks of 4.26% and 5.54% [E9, E10]. Furthermore, fears regarding operational momentum ignore massive multi-year expansion, driven by a 3-year compounded sales growth of 290% and a 3-year compounded profit growth of 376% [E14, E16]. Conceded: operating margins read inconsistent [E25, E26] and the 1-year share price growth is -11% with the stock below its moving averages [E20, E41]; nevertheless, the business trades at an attractive P/E of 11.8x to 12.05x compared to the sector benchmark of 22.38x [E1, E6], backed by a rules-based screen score of 75 out of 100 [E48].

Conceded: the company displays high multi-year compounded sales growth of 290% and profit growth of 376% alongside strong reported ROE and ROCE figures that outperform sector benchmarks [E9, E10, E14, E16]. However, relying on these accounting returns ignores severe underlying quality concerns, specifically the flag that the company might be capitalizing its interest cost [E47]. This aggressive accounting treatment coincides with an alarming deterioration in cash generation, evidenced by negative operating cash flow of Rs -38 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -39 Cr for March 2026, resulting in a disastrous cash conversion ratio of -0.72x [E27, E28, E29]. Furthermore, the bull's dismissal of balance sheet risks is undermined by rising borrowings reaching Rs 262 Cr, which drive the debt-to-equity ratio to 1.98x where debt exceeds net worth [E30, E32]. Finally, the claim of an attractive valuation ignores clear technical warning signs, as the stock sits below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages and has suffered a 1-year share price decline of -11% [E20, E41].
